name: PowerView Interesting File & Share ACL Hunting
description: Search readable domain shares for files whose names match sensitive patterns (passwords, configs, scripts, keys) and inspect the ACLs on file paths. The PowerView-native equivalent of Snaffler - finds credentials and secrets sitting on shares without dropping a tool on disk.

variations.label: Search a specific path for interesting files
variations.description: Uses PowerView to crawl accessible network shares looking for sensitive files (configs, scripts, passwords, private keys). Searches file names and extensions for common patterns that indicate credential exposure.

variations.label: ACLs on a filesystem path (SYSVOL / share perms)
variations.description: ACLs on a filesystem path (SYSVOL / share perms). See the command syntax for exact parameters and flags.

variations.label: Find reachable domain shares first
variations.description: Discovers network shares across domain computers. Identifies accessible file shares for data mining, credential harvesting, and finding writable deployment shares.

notes: Find-InterestingFile / Find-InterestingDomainShareFile need read access to the target path; full coverage of admin-only shares (C$, ADMIN$) requires local admin. Get-PathAcl needs local admin only when reading ACLs on a remote machine's filesystem. Common finds: unattend.xml, web.config, sysprep.inf, .kdbx, .ps1 scripts with hardcoded creds, Groups.xml (GPP cpassword).

defense.why_it_works: Any authenticated user can enumerate shares and read files their ACLs permit. Organisations routinely leave credentials, config files, and scripts on shares readable by 'Authenticated Users' or 'Domain Users', so a domain account is enough to loot secrets.
defense.prerequisites: Any valid domain account. SMB (445) to file servers. Read access on the target shares (local admin only for admin$ shares).
defense.impact: T1083/T1135/T1039 discovery + T1552.001 credentials in files. Plaintext or reversible credentials recovered from shares frequently yield privileged accounts and immediate escalation.
defense.misconfiguration: Over-permissive share/NTFS ACLs (Authenticated Users: Read). Credentials stored in cleartext in scripts/configs on shares. GPP cpassword left in SYSVOL. No file-access auditing.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Share readable by all domain users, contains creds:
# \\fileserver\IT\scripts\deploy.ps1  ->  $pass = 'P@ssw0rd123'
# ACL: BUILTIN\Users Allow Read
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict share ACLs to least privilege:
Get-SmbShareAccess -Name 'IT'
Revoke-SmbShareAccess -Name 'IT' -AccountName 'Authenticated Users' -Force
Grant-SmbShareAccess -Name 'IT' -AccountName 'CORP\IT-Staff' -AccessRight Read -Force
# Remove secrets from shares; use a vault (LAPS/gMSA/CyberArk). Purge GPP cpassword (KB2962486).
defense.detection: Mass SMB reads / directory enumeration across many shares from one host (Sysmon 3 + Windows 5140/5145 share-access auditing). MDI 'Data exfiltration/enumeration' analytics. Honeyfiles with named-pipe/canary alerts on access.
defense.artifacts: Event 5140/5145 (network share access) bursts | Sysmon 3 to 445 many hosts | Access to canary/honeyfiles
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5145 (Relative_Target_Name="*pass*" OR Relative_Target_Name="*.config" OR Relative_Target_Name="*.xml")
| stats dc(Computer) as hosts count by Account_Name, Source_Address
| where hosts>5

index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText="*Find-InterestingDomainShareFile*"
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5145 and (RelativeTargetName has "pass" or RelativeTargetName endswith ".config" or RelativeTargetName endswith ".xml")
| summarize hosts=dcount(Computer), count() by SubjectUserName, IpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where hosts > 5
| sort by count_ desc
defense.prevention: Least-privilege share ACLs; remove cleartext secrets from shares; deploy LAPS/gMSA; enable object-access auditing (5145); deploy honeyfiles; purge GPP cpassword.
defense.evasion: Target a curated host/share list instead of the whole domain; filter by extension to reduce reads; run during business hours to blend with normal file activity.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log, PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Sysmon for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Check for credential dumping artifacts (LSASS access, SAM hive reads, Kerberos anomalies)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
The PowerView-native equivalent of Snaffler - finds secrets sitting on domain shares:
  Find-InterestingDomainShareFile   walk readable shares for files matching name patterns
  -Include *pass*,*.config,*.xml,*.vbs,*.ps1   the sensitive filename patterns to flag
Run Find-DomainShare -CheckShareAccess first to know which shares you can read, then inspect promising hits with Get-PathAcl. Often surfaces cleartext creds in scripts/configs.
